locator.section: RG 480–481, 511 d/i, 513–514; Ordo Missae rubric and chant formula after the secrets

entries.claim: The final secret has an audible Per omnia saecula saeculorum followed by the response Amen. Collects and postcommunions are priestly orations with a separate response. These rules determine the modeled boundaries, not the completeness of a date-specific commemoration inventory.

The same-edition Son-directed common conclusion in Rubricae generales 115 d ends with the printed word Amen. It supplies the Latin wording of the reader’s separate w037 response after the expanded Qui vivis conclusion. This use does not establish the response performer, voice or date-specific liturgical applicability; those are distinct ritual claims.

The prescribed conclusion for a prayer addressed to the Son supplies the expanded Qui vivis et regnas through per omnia saecula saeculorum (w021–w036), while the proper page prints only the opening cue. Reader accentuation is supplied separately.

The cited page prints this Postcommunion’s proper body and the abbreviated conclusion “Qui vivis”. The full conclusion follows Rubricae generales 115 d, with reader-supplied accentuation. Amen is shown separately as a response. The proper page does not print the full conclusion or that response.
